mainTopic: The torch signals, the witnesses' courtyard and their walking rights on שבת, and how witnesses to the new moon were questioned
overview: This amud finishes the torch signals for ראש חודש. בית בלתין is identified as בירם. The גולה that looked like a bonfire is פומבדיתא, where everyone held a torch on his roof. A ברייתא adds more stations, and רבי יוחנן says the stations were eight פרסאות apart. אביי explains that the trip is longer today because the direct roads were blocked, and two פסוקים are brought for this. A new משנה describes בית יעזק, the courtyard where witnesses were hosted with big meals. It also tells how רבן גמליאל הזקן let them, and also midwives and rescuers, walk 2,000 אמות on שבת. The גמרא asks whether the name is בית יעזק or בית יזק, and the question is not settled. Another משנה describes how the witnesses were questioned about the moon. אביי explains that 'in front of the sun' asks which way the moon's hollow side faced. רבי יוחנן supports this with a פסוק, and his reason about the rainbow continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית בלתין is בירם
steps.stepSummary: The last torch station in the משנה, בית בלתין, is identified as a place called בירם.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is בירם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question, 'What is בית בלתין?', by saying it is the town called בירם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed the mountains where torches were waved, ending with בית בלתין. The גמרא gives that last station its more familiar name, so we know where the chain of signals ended.

keyTerms.meaning: Biram, the place identified as בית בלתין

phrases.english: This is Biram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun before this section

steps.title: What does 'Diaspora' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by the word גולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the 'Diaspora'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what place the משנה means when it says the person on the last station saw the whole גולה lit up. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One person on a mountain could not see the entire Jewish world outside ארץ ישראל. So the word גולה must mean one specific place, and the גמרא wants to know which.

keyTerms.meaning: the Diaspora, Jewish communities outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: What is the 'Diaspora'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next unclear word in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which place the משנה means by גולה

steps.title: The גולה here means פומבדיתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the גולה is the city of פומבדיתא in Bavel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is פומבדיתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that the משנה's גולה is פומבדיתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last torch station was בית בלתין (step 1). The person waving there would see the city of פומבדיתא lit up in front of him. That one central city of the Babylonian Jews is what 'the גולה' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: Pumbedita, a major Jewish city in Bavel

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: This is Pumbedita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 2

steps.title: What does 'like a bonfire' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the city looked like one big bonfire.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'like a bonfire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means when it says the גולה looked like a bonfire. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole city would not be one actual fire. The גמרא wants to know what the people did that made it look that way.

keyTerms.meaning: a bonfire, a big pile of burning wood

phrases.english: What is 'like a bonfire'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the next phrase of the same משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the city came to look like one bonfire

steps.title: Everyone held a torch on his roof
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that every person took a torch and went up on his roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Each and every person takes a torch in his hand and goes up to the top of his roof.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains that every person in the city stood on his roof holding a torch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With so many torches burning on every roof at once, the whole city glowed like one huge fire. This is how the people of the גולה joined in announcing the new month.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The גולה in the משנה is פומבדיתא, and it 'looked like a bonfire' because everyone stood on his roof with a torch.

phrases.english: It was taught: each and every one
takes a torch in his hand
and goes up to the top of his roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹטֵל אֲבוּקָה בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each person lit a torch on his roof, so the city looked like one bonfire

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds more stations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר lists more torch stations: חרים, כייר, גדר and nearby places.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: Also חרים and כייר and גדר and its neighboring places.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says torches were also waved at other places not named in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה named five stations. This ברייתא adds more, which raises a question the גמרא answers next: where were these extra places?

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
its neighbors, the places near it

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Also Charim and Kayar
and Geder and its neighboring places.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: אַף חָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that adds to the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torches were also waved at חרים, כייר, גדר and nearby places

steps.title: First view: the extra stations were in between
steps.stepSummary: Some say the places רבי שמעון בן אלעזר added stood between the stations of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: They stood in between.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first explanation of where the extra stations were: between the stations listed in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, the ברייתא is adding extra stops inside the same chain. So the משנה and ברייתא describe the same route, and the ברייתא just fills in more points.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בֵּינֵי וּבֵינֵי הֲווֹ קָיְימִי.
phrases.english: Some say: they were located in between.
phrases.notes: He means between the mountains the משנה named.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בֵּינֵי וּבֵינֵי הֲווֹ קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where the places in step 6 were
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra stations stood between the משנה's stations

steps.title: Second view: the extra stations were on the other side
steps.stepSummary: Others say the extra stations were on the far side of ארץ ישראל, so each source lists a different side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: They stood on the other side of ארץ ישראל. One Sage counts this side, and one Sage counts that side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation: the extra places were on the other side of ארץ ישראל, and each source lists the stations of a different side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this view, the משנה and the ברייתא are not arguing at all. Each one simply names the stations on a different side, so together they describe the whole route.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: לְהָךְ גִּיסָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲווֹ קָיְימִי.
phrases.english: they were located on the other side of Eretz Yisrael.
One Sage counts the places on this side,
phrases.notes: One 'Sage' is the משנה and the other is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and the other Sage counts the places on that side.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: לְהָךְ גִּיסָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל הֲווֹ קָיְימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different location for the same extra stations
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra stations were on the other side; the משנה and ברייתא each list one side

steps.title: Eight פרסאות between each station
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says each torch station was eight פרסאות from the next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Between each and every one there were eight פרסאות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us the distance between one torch station and the next: eight פרסאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a measurement to the משנה's chain of stations. The גמרא will now add up the total and test it against what people know about the route.

keyTerms.meaning: a leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
a parsah, a long measure of distance

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Between each and every one
there were eight parsaos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בֵּין כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת שְׁמוֹנֶה פַּרְסָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point about distances
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each station was eight פרסאות from the next

steps.title: How far is the whole route?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the total distance comes to.
steps.simpleTranslation: How much do they come to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how many פרסאות the whole route adds up to. This sets up a calculation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the distance per station, we can add up the full trip from הר המשחה to בית בלתין.

phrases.english: How much do they come to?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's number
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The total distance of the route

steps.title: The total is thirty-two פרסאות
steps.stepSummary: The total comes to thirty-two פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Thirty-two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the whole route is thirty-two פרסאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה named five stations, which makes four gaps between them. Four gaps of eight פרסאות each come to thirty-two.

phrases.english: Thirty-two.
phrases.notes: Five stations means four gaps, and four times eight is thirty-two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10

steps.title: But today the route is much longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: nowadays the trip is much more than thirty-two פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But today they are much more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's number, because people in its own time know the trip is much longer than thirty-two פרסאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the stations were eight פרסאות apart, the route should be thirty-two. But real travelers find it much longer, so the number seems wrong.

phrases.english: But nowadays they are much more!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the total just calculated
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's eight פרסאות per station
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The known travel distance today is much more than thirty-two פרסאות

steps.title: The direct roads became blocked
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the straight roads were blocked, so today's travelers must take longer routes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The roads have become blocked to them.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי יוחנן: the short, direct roads have been closed, so people now go a longer way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The straight-line distance really is thirty-two פרסאות. The trip only feels longer today because travelers can't use the direct roads anymore.
steps.whatToRemember: The stations were eight פרסאות apart, thirty-two in total. Today's longer trip is because the direct roads are blocked, not because the number is wrong.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The roads have become blocked to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִסְתַּתּוֹמֵי אִסְתַּתּוּם לְהוּ דַּרְכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's distance doesn't match the real route
steps.terutzMaskana: The direct distance is thirty-two פרסאות; today's routes are longer because the direct roads are blocked

steps.title: A פסוק showing the roads were blocked
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from הושע to back up אביי's claim that the old roads were blocked.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Therefore, behold, I will hedge up your way with thorns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as a source for אביי's answer that the straight roads were blocked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 אביי explained that the trip is longer today because the direct roads were closed off. Here the פסוק says ה' will block the people's way with thorns, which supports the idea that the old paths are no longer usable.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written; introduces a פסוק

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Therefore, behold, I will hedge up'
your way with thorns.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לָכֵן הִנְנִי שָׂךְ אֶת דַּרְכֵּךְ בַּסִּירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for אביי's answer in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the straight roads to ירושלים were blocked.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 2:8, 'I will hedge up your way with thorns.'

steps.title: A second source for the longer roads
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a different פסוק from איכה to show the paths became crooked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We learn it from here, as it is written: 'He has made my paths crooked.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers another פסוק as the source for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the idea that today's routes are longer. He just learns it from a different פסוק: paths that were made 'crooked' are no longer straight, so the trip takes longer.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives another source
From here; introduces a different source

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא,
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: from here,
as it is written: 'He has made my paths crooked.'

steps.whatToRemember: The trip is longer today because the old straight roads were blocked or bent. Two פסוקים are given as sources: הושע (thorns block the way) and איכה (crooked paths).
steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same point made in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that today's routes are longer than the original straight roads.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איכה 3:9, 'He has made my paths crooked.'

steps.title: The courtyard where witnesses gathered
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes בית יעזק, the large courtyard in ירושלים where new-moon witnesses gathered, were checked, and were given big meals.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a large courtyard in ירושלים called בית יעזק. All the witnesses gathered there, and בית דין checked them there. They made big meals for them so that they would get used to coming.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes the place where witnesses about the new moon came and how they were treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who saw the new moon had to come to ירושלים and be checked by בית דין. To make sure people would keep coming, they were hosted with big meals, so that coming to testify would feel normal and welcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
The name of the courtyard where witnesses gathered
Witnesses, here people who saw the new moon
Used to, in the habit of

phrases.english: MISHNAH: There was a large courtyard in Jerusalem,
and it was called Beit Ya'zek,
and all the witnesses would gather there.
And the court would examine them there.
And they would make big meals for them,
so that they would be used to coming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the end of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses gathered in בית יעזק, were examined there by בית דין, and were given big meals to encourage them to come.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל lets witnesses walk on שבת
steps.stepSummary: At first, witnesses who arrived on שבת could not leave the courtyard all day; רבן גמליאל הזקן made a rule that they may walk 2,000 אמות in every direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, they would not move from there the whole day. רבן גמליאל הזקן made a rule that they could walk 2,000 אמות in every direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells about a change: witnesses used to be stuck in the courtyard all day, and רבן גמליאל הזקן made a תקנה to let them walk around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who came on שבת from far away had gone past their walking limit, so they could not walk around freely. Being stuck all day was a reason not to come, so רבן גמליאל gave them a full 2,000 אמות from where they were, like a person who lives there.

keyTerms.meaning: 2,000 אמות, the normal שבת walking limit

phrases.english: At first, they would not move
phrases.notes: The משנה assumes these witnesses came on שבת from far away, past the normal walking limit.

phrases.english: from there the whole day.
Rabban Gamliel the Elder made a rule

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהוּ מְהַלְּכִין אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה לְכׇל רוּחַ.
phrases.english: that they may walk 2,000 cubits in every direction.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חכמים made rules to make it easy for witnesses to come, because their testimony was needed to set the calendar.
steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה לֹא הָיוּ זָזִין מִשָּׁם כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה about how witnesses were treated, adding a rule about walking on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who arrived on שבת may walk 2,000 אמות in every direction from where they are.

steps.title: The same rule for a midwife and rescuers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that a midwife and anyone who comes to save people are treated like the people of the town and get 2,000 אמות in every direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only these witnesses. Also a midwife who comes to deliver a baby, and someone who comes to save people from a fire, from an army, from a river, or from a collapsed building: they are like the people of the town and have 2,000 אמות in every direction.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens רבן גמליאל's rule beyond witnesses to other people who travel on שבת to help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the witnesses, these people go past their walking limit on שבת for a needed reason. So that they won't hold back, they are treated like the people living in the town they came to, and they get a full 2,000 אמות from there.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the people who live in the town

phrases.english: And not only these,
but also a midwife who comes to deliver a baby,
and one who comes to rescue from a fire,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַגַּיִיס וּמִן הַנָּהָר וּמִן הַמַּפּוֹלֶת —
phrases.english: from troops, from a river, or from a collapse —
these are like the people of the town,
and they have 2,000 cubits in every direction.

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses, a midwife, and rescuers who arrive on שבת are treated like the people of that town and may walk 2,000 אמות in every direction.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא אֵלּוּ בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא אַף חֲכָמָה הַבָּאָה לְיַילֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule from step 17 to other people who travel on שבת to help.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A midwife and anyone coming to rescue from fire, troops, a river, or a collapse are like the town's residents and get 2,000 אמות in every direction.

steps.title: How is the courtyard's name read?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה says בית יעזק, a positive name, or בית יזק, a name that sounds like suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: did we learn 'בית יעזק' or 'בית יזק'? If it is בית יעזק, that is a positive word, like the פסוק 'he dug it and cleared it of stones.' Or maybe it is בית יזק, a word of pain, like the פסוק 'he was bound in chains.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the exact wording of the משנה: what was the courtyard's name? Each possible reading is backed by a word from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two readings differ by one letter, but they give opposite feelings. בית יעזק comes from a root meaning care and improvement, so it fits a place where witnesses were treated well. בית יזק comes from אזיקים, chains, so it fits witnesses who were stuck in the courtyard all שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים
An expression of pain or distress

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was asked to them:
Did we learn "Beit Ya'zek,"
or did we learn "Beit Yazek"?
Did we learn "Beit Ya'zek" —
which is a fine, positive word,
as it is written: "And he dug it and cleared it of stones"
or perhaps we learned "Beit Yazek" —
which is a word of distress,
as it is written: "And he was bound in chains"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה from steps 16-18 by asking about the courtyard's exact name.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the courtyard's name in the משנה is the positive בית יעזק or the distressing בית יזק.

steps.title: אביי's proof from the big meals
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the משנה says the witnesses were given big meals, which suggests the positive name בית יעזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear. The משנה says they made big meals for the witnesses there, so they would be used to coming.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tries to answer the question by pointing to the meals mentioned in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses were served big meals, the place was treated as a pleasant spot. That fits the positive name בית יעזק better than a name about chains.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof is being brought)
Used to coming, so they will come again

phrases.english: Abaye said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: סְעוּדוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין לָהֶם שָׁם,
phrases.english: They would make big meals for them there,
so that they would be used to coming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: He tries to settle the question from step 19 by using the line about the meals from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The reading בית יעזק, a positive name
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's line that big meals were made for the witnesses

steps.title: Maybe they did both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the witnesses may have been given meals and also been restricted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe they did two things to them: they fed them well, and they also kept them stuck there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meals do not rule out the unpleasant side, because the witnesses who came on שבת still could not leave the courtyard. Since both could be true, the meals do not prove which name is right, and the question is left open.

phrases.english: Perhaps they did two things with them.
phrases.notes: He means they got good meals and were also not allowed to leave the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects אביי's proof from step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question of the name is not decided either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The meals and the restriction could both be true, so the meals cannot decide the name.

steps.title: Questioning the first witness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that the first pair is checked first. The senior witness is asked detailed questions about where the moon was and what it looked like.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do they check the witnesses? The pair that came first is checked first. They bring in the senior one and ask: Tell us how you saw the moon. Was it in front of the sun or behind it? North or south of it? How high was it, which way was it tilted, and how wide was it? If he says it was in front of the sun, his testimony is worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה describes how בית דין questions the first witness of the first pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses are questioned one at a time, with very specific questions about the moon's position and shape. That way the court can later see whether the two accounts match. Some answers, like 'in front of the sun,' are impossible for a new moon, so they show right away that the witness is wrong or lying.

keyTerms.meaning: He said nothing, so his testimony is worthless

steps.confusionAlert: Don't decide yet what 'in front of the sun' means. In step 24 the גמרא asks how it differs from 'north or south.' In step 25 אביי explains that it is about which way the moon's hollow side faces, and that side can never face the sun.

phrases.english: MISHNA: How do they examine the witnesses?
The pair that came first —
they examine it first.
And they bring in the greater of the two,
and they say to him,
Tell us how you saw the moon:
In front of the sun, or behind the sun?
To its north, or to its south?
How high was it,
and which way was it tilting,
and how wide was it?
If he said, "in front of the sun" —
he has said nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the courtyard's name, a new משנה moves on to how the witnesses gathered there were questioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first pair is examined first, one witness at a time, starting with the senior one, using detailed questions about the moon. An impossible answer cancels the testimony.

steps.title: The second witness and the other pairs
steps.stepSummary: The second witness is questioned. If the two accounts match, the testimony stands. The other pairs are asked only general questions, so they do not leave disappointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then they bring in the second witness and check him. If their words match, their testimony stands. All the other pairs are asked only the main points. This is not because the court needs them, but so they will not leave feeling let down, and so they will keep coming in the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the questioning: it compares the two witnesses, then explains how the extra pairs are treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two matching accounts are enough to accept the testimony, so the other pairs are not really needed. The court still asks them general questions out of respect, so that they feel their trip mattered and will come again next time.

keyTerms.meaning: Matching, lining up with each other

steps.whatToRemember: Two witnesses whose detailed answers match are enough. Extra witnesses get a short, respectful hearing so they will keep coming. This is the same reason given for the big meals.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows again how much בית דין worked to keep witnesses willing to come. The same goal, שיהו רגילים לבוא, appeared earlier with the meals.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיוּ מַכְנִיסִין אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: And afterward they would bring in the second one
and examine him.
If their words are found to match —
their testimony stands.
And all the other pairs,
they ask them the main points.
Not because they needed them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יֵצְאוּ בְּפַחֵי נֶפֶשׁ,
phrases.english: but so that they would not leave disappointed,
so that they would be used to coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיוּ מַכְנִיסִין אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It continues the questioning from step 22 with the second witness and the extra pairs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Matching accounts from the first pair are accepted. The other pairs get only general questions, so they will not be discouraged from coming again.

steps.title: Aren't two of the questions the same?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: 'in front of the sun' means the same as 'north of it', and 'behind the sun' means the same as 'south of it', so why ask both?
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Being in front of the sun is the same as being north of it, and being behind the sun is the same as being south of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by attacking the list of questions the court asks the witnesses. It says two of the questions seem to repeat each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had the court ask whether the moon was before or behind the sun, and also whether it was north or south of it. The גמרא assumes both questions are about the moon's position. If so, they ask the same thing in different words, and the second question adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: To its north / to its south

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"In front of the sun" is the same as "to its north";
phrases.notes: These are questions from the משנה in Step 22, which the court asks the senior witness.

phrases.english: "behind the sun" is the same as "to its south"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's discussion of the questions in the משנה from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's list of questions for the senior witness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two of the questions seem to mean the same thing, so one of them is unnecessary.

steps.title: אביי: the question is about which way the curve faces
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'before or behind the sun' asks which way the moon's concave side faced. If the witness says it faced the sun, his testimony is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The question is whether its concave side faced the sun or faced away from it. If the witness said it faced the sun, he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. He says the first question is not about where the moon was, but about which way its curved-in edge was facing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'north or south' question is about the moon's position. The 'before or behind the sun' question is about its shape, meaning the direction its hollow side points. So the two questions are different. A witness who says the hollow side faced the sun is giving a description that is impossible, so his testimony counts for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Its gap, meaning the curved-in (hollow) side of the crescent moon
He has said nothing, meaning his testimony is worthless

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Its concave side — was it facing the sun,
or facing away from the sun?
If he said it was facing the sun,
he has said nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: פְּגִימָתָהּ — לִפְנֵי הַחַמָּה, אוֹ לְאַחַר הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting what the question is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both questions ask about the moon's position, so they repeat each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: One question asks about position (north or south). The other asks about which way the hollow side faces. A witness who says it faced the sun is not believed.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Before the sun' here does not mean the moon's location. It means the hollow side of the crescent was pointing toward the sun.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the sun never sees the concave side
steps.stepSummary: Support for אביי from רבי יוחנן, who explains a פסוק in איוב as teaching that the sun never sees the concave side of the moon or of a rainbow.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: What is the meaning of the פסוק 'Dominion and fear are with Him, He makes peace in His high places'? The sun has never seen the concave side of the moon, nor the concave side of a rainbow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי יוחנן to prove אביי's point that the hollow side of the moon can never face the sun.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'He makes peace in His high places' as a description of how the heavens are arranged. The hollow side of the moon and of a rainbow always points away from the sun. This is why a witness who says the hollow side faced the sun must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes peace in His high places

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Dominion and fear are with Him,
He makes peace in His high places"?
The sun has never seen
the concave side of the moon,
nor the concave side of a rainbow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for אביי's claim in Step 25.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that a witness who says the concave side faced the sun has said nothing

steps.title: The reasons: the moon's feelings and the sun-worshippers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains why: the moon would feel hurt if the sun saw its concave side, and for the rainbow, so the sun-worshippers would not say something. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sun never sees the concave side of the moon, because the moon would feel bad. It never sees the concave side of a rainbow, so that the sun-worshippers should not say...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a separate reason for the moon and for the rainbow. His sentence about the rainbow continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the moon, the reason is the 'peace' in the פסוק: the moon would feel small if the sun saw its weak, hollow side. For the rainbow, the reason has to do with what sun-worshippers might claim, and the rest of that reason comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Because she would feel discouraged or hurt
So that they should not say

phrases.english: The concave side of the moon [the sun never sees] —
because she would feel bad.
The concave side of a rainbow [the sun never sees] —
so that the sun-worshippers should not say

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind רבי יוחנן's statement in Step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun never sees the moon's concave side so the moon will not feel hurt, and never sees the rainbow's concave side so sun-worshippers will not make a claim (the claim comes next).
